note.p: Verse KM-S-1 below is a good-faith transcription of the opening invocatory verse (folio 1, addressed to Vikaṭacakravināyaka) of the real 1889 printed Śaiva Kāñcīmāhātmya described in , read directly from the digitised page image by the encoder, who is not a trained Sanskritist. Word-division, several akṣaras — notably mekarasālino in line 1b, whose intended sense is unclear to the encoder — and the exact anusvāra/visarga marks of the printed Telugu script should be treated as provisional pending review by a qualified reader; corrections are welcome. The Devanāgarī given is a script-normalised rendering of a Telugu-script original (see ), not a diplomatic transliteration of individual glyphs. A second invocatory verse is visible on the same folio but was not legible enough to the encoder to transcribe responsibly, and has been left out rather than guessed at. Beyond this one verse, the file's remaining apparatus machinery (parallel-segmentation app/lem/rdg, further chapters) is demonstration scaffolding illustrating the encoding model, not a transcription of further text; see encoding guidelines, section "Replacing the sample corpus".

The @corresp links that formerly pointed from this file's synthetic verses to KP-ch1/KP-1/KM-S-2 have been removed (2026-09-20). kanchippuranam.xml carries a real 50-verse excerpt of Civañāna Munivar's Kāñcippurāṇam (a genuine sthalapuranam about Kanchipuram); this file's one real verse (KM-S-1, added 2026-09-20) is an opening maṅgala invocation to Gaṇeśa, not sthalapuranam content about Kanchipuram itself, so no verse-level correspondence to the Tamil text is asserted yet. Once more of the Śaiva Kāñcīmāhātmya's narrative chapters (adhyāyas 2 onward, per ) are transcribed, a genuine @corresp alignment to kanchippuranam.xml can be re-added where an actual correspondence is verified.

bibl.title: Śrīkāñcīmāhātmyagranthaḥ: śrīskāndapurāṇāntargataḥ śrīrudrakoṭimahimādarśaḥ
bibl.note: Title page subtitle: nānādeśasamānītagrandhacatuṣṭayāvalokanapūrvakam ("prepared after comparing four texts collected from various regions") — the print is itself a collation of earlier exemplars, not a copy of a single manuscript.

Printed in Telugu script. Digitised by Heidelberg University Library for the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities project "Hindu Temple Legends in South India" (Pondicherry unit), from a copy held at the Institut français de Pondichéry (IFP); no shelfmark is given by the digitiser.

availability.p: The digital reproduction is rights-flagged "In Copyright" by Heidelberg University Library, reflecting the library's standard reproduction policy for its scanned holdings, not a claim that the underlying 1889 publication remains under copyright. No claim of rights is made here over the 1889 text; only the single-page facsimile image linked in the file's facsimile element is referenced, at the resolution the image server itself serves.

witness.desc: The 1889 printed edition described above; the only witness actually consulted for this file. Its own title page states it was compiled from four exemplars gathered from various regions, but those underlying exemplars are not independently accessible to the encoder, so no apparatus of variant readings is given here — this is a diplomatic reading of the collated print, not a critical apparatus.

projectDesc.p: Demonstration of a TEI-based editorial pipeline for South Indian temple legends, built to illustrate eXist-db, RESTXQ, XSLT and Linked Open Data integration.

prefixDef.p: References of the form authority:place-kanchipuram resolve to entries in the shared authority file.

normalization.p: All Indic text is stored in Unicode NFC. Devanāgarī is the storage script for Sanskrit; IAST transliteration is generated, not hand-keyed.

revisionDesc.change: Removed @corresp links to kanchippuranam.xml, which now carries real (not synthetic) verse text unrelated to this file's placeholder content; see the added alignment note.

Located a real, publicly accessible digitised source for the Śaiva Kāñcīmāhātmya (1889 print, Heidelberg/IFP, DOI 10.11588/diglit.72555) and replaced the placeholder sourceDesc/listWit/facsimile with its real bibliographic details and page image. Transcribed its opening invocatory verse (folio 1, to Vikaṭacakravināyaka) as KM-S-1, a good-faith non-expert reading with caveats recorded in the provenance-warning note; dropped the second placeholder verse (KM-S-2) and the fabricated multi-witness apparatus, since only one real witness has actually been consulted.

zone.note: Approximate region of verse KM-S-1 (the two lines beginning svakaṭajāta-), estimated from IIIF crops; not pixel-exact.

div.head: श्रीस्कान्दपुराणान्तर्गतकाञ्चीमाहात्म्यप्रारम्भः
div.note: Rubric and verse below transcribed from folio 1 of witness E1889 (see ); see the file's provenance-warning note for caveats. No entities from this corpus's authority file (Kanchipuram, Śiva, Kāmākṣī) appear in this opening Gaṇeśa invocation, so no persName/placeName links are attached here.
